subject: Immediate: production regressions after v4.2 / q8mix rollout (OpalWorks)
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@opalworks.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: OpalWorks SRE <ops@opalworks.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Production regressions observed immediately after v4.2-q8mix rollout

Jordan —

We just finished the automated rollout of Redwood model v4.2 with the q8mix quantization profile across our US cluster at 08:45 PDT and saw a rapid degradation in request success rate and latency. Current summary (first 20 minutes):

- p95 latency went from ~220ms -> ~1.1s
- p99 latency spiked from ~480ms -> ~2.8s
- 5xx error rate at edge jumped to ~3.8% (was ~0.2% baseline)
- sustained throughput collapsed ~30% under normal load despite steady request volume

We rolled to a partial canary and observed the same behavior, so we halted the rollout and the issue persisted on the canary nodes. Attached: p99 chart, targeted logs, and qprofile used.

This is customer-impacting for several critical endpoints (summarization and chat). We need an immediate rollback or a mitigation path. Can you advise on next steps and whether you can flip back to the previous model variant (v4.1 / q16) from your side?

Samir
OpalWorks — Head of Platform

Attachments: p99-latency-chart-20270803.png (image), prod-system-logs-20270803.tar.gz (text bundle)

Also: do you have an automated rollback we can trigger from our control plane to return OpalWorks to v4.1/q16 while we investigate?

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: quick triage + propose safe rollback path (flip or route 100% to v4.1)
- Evelyn: FYI for potential exec loop and credits communication
- Samir: please confirm whether OpalWorks applied any client-side changes at the same time (timeouts, new batching).

I’ll coordinate the customer comms and keep you posted every 30 minutes.

—Jordan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Production regressions observed immediately after v4.2-q8mix rollout

Quick update from infra/model-ops perspective — findings so far (10:00 PDT):

- Reproduced p99 latency and 5xx spike on a local repro using v4.2 + q8mix under a synthetic traffic profile that matches OpalWorks’ request shape (longer prefixes, repeated long-context requests).
- Observation: q8mix (hybrid 8-bit mixed-block quant) appears to increase L2 cache pressure and leads to intermittent kernel stalls when sequence length > 1024 with dense KV-cache hits. This only surfaces on our newer A100-optimized kernel set when a specific block alignment pattern is present.
- NVMe/ephemeral swap wasn’t the immediate cause; disk metrics are normal. The stacktrace points to a GPU kernel launch order deadlock in our fused-attention path that manifests as timeouts at the serving proxy layer.

Short-term mitigations we can execute now (ordered by speed/risk):
1) Route OpalWorks traffic off nodes running the q8mix profile and back to v4.1/q16 binary (we can flip routing at the control plane; risk: transient connection churn). Estimated time: ~12–20 minutes to reach 95% routing swap.
2) Enable a per-customer soft-fallback: detect >1% 5xx and auto-route to v4.1 for new sessions (can be enabled in ~8 minutes).
3) Apply a kernel patch to add a protective serialization for the fused-attention path (non-disruptive but needs rolling restart of affected nodes; ETA 3–5 hours).

I recommend (1) + (2) immediately for OpalWorks, then hold the kernel patch for a scheduled maintenance window after a postmortem. We can also push a full rollback if OpalWorks prefers; we have the v4.1 artifacts ready.

I’m starting the routing flip now and will post progress to INF-8932.

—Marcus
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Please prioritize OpalWorks as a P1 incident. Include a clear timeline and next touchpoints.

—Evelyn

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Mehta <anita.mehta@opalworks.ai>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@opalworks.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, OpalWorks SRE <ops@opalworks.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood: Immediate remediation + next steps (OpalWorks production regression)

Anita —

First, I want to apologize for the impact you saw this morning after we rolled v4.2 with the q8mix profile. We take incidents like this very seriously. Summary of what we’ve done so far and next steps: 

1) What happened (short): v4.2 with the new q8mix quantization profile produced an unexpected kernel interaction under OpalWorks’ request shapes, which increased p99 latency and caused a small but visible 5xx spike across affected endpoints.

2) Immediate remediation (completed):
- At 10:10 PDT we routed OpalWorks traffic away from nodes running q8mix and returned traffic to the previously validated v4.1/q16 binary. This reduced p99 back toward baseline within ~18 minutes.
- We also enabled a soft-fallback rule for OpalWorks to auto-route any sessions that exceed 1% 5xx to v4.1.

3) Observed impact:
- p99 dropped to ~300–400ms within 20 minutes of remediation. Error rates reduced to ~0.3%.
- Throughput normalized after routing swap; no data loss detected.

4) Next steps:
- We’ll complete a kernel patch and roll a non-disruptive fix (ETA 3–5 hours) and run a targeted canary with OpalWorks traffic only when you approve.
- We’ll run a full postmortem and share it within 48 hours, including root cause, corrective actions, and mitigations to prevent recurrence.

5) Commercial remediation:
- We propose a one-time service credit proportional to the minutes of elevated error/latency; we’ll formalize this in follow-up once you confirm the impacted SLA windows.

Attached: incident ticket INF-8932 (link), p99 chart, logs we analyzed. We’ll be available for a call anytime this afternoon to walk through the technicals.

I’m very sorry for the disruption — we’ll follow through and keep you updated every hour until resolved.

—Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-playbook-OpalWorks.md (text), p99-latency-chart-20270803.png (image)
From: Anita Mehta <anita.mehta@opalworks.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood: Immediate remediation + next steps (OpalWorks production regression)

Jordan / Team —

Thank you for the fast response and for routing us back to the prior variant; we saw the latency improvements and appreciate the clear next steps. A couple quick asks: 

- Please share the postmortem and kernel patch notes (INF-8932) as soon as available.
- We’d like a brief technical call tomorrow morning (09:00 PDT) with Marcus and someone from model-ops to review the patch plan and canary gating criteria.
- Regarding credits: please send a proposed credit amount and the SLA windows you’re calculating from.

We’ll hold on any client-side changes; no changes were made on our end during the window.

Anita Mehta
CTO, OpalWorks
